prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how many units of each parent category were sold through each channel in the first quarter of 2025 (order_date from 1 January 2025 to 31 March 2025, both days included)? Use the sales table. Return three columns, in this order: parent_category, channel and units_sold, the sum of units. Return one row per parent_category and channel combination. Order lines with missing units add nothing to the total. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per parent_category and channel combination

hints: Next, decide what one row stands for, then compare the plain columns in the SELECT list with the GROUP BY list.
Every column in the SELECT list that is not inside SUM must also be in GROUP BY. One of them is missing there, so the engine stops with an error.
starter_sql:
SELECT parent_category, channel, SUM(units) AS units_sold
FROM sales
WHERE order_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-03-31'
GROUP BY parent_category
why_this_works: GROUP BY parent_category, channel makes one group per combination, so channel can stand next to the total.
